claims.statement: 186 orders allocated overnight to east node are stuck in 'allocated, awaiting pickup' since 06:00
claims.corroboration: Confirmed by both observability alert (9% of overnight allocations) and fulfillment report (every held order was routed to east node)
claims.limitation: Observation confirms the state, not the cause

claims.statement: All 186 stuck orders are flagged as split-reservation exceptions
claims.corroboration: Fulfillment report explicitly states all held orders flagged by overnight allocator as split-reservation exception
claims.limitation: Exception flag existence confirmed; does not explain why they remain stuck (downstream processing issue vs. root rule defect)

claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 went live at 22:00 and reserves stock from east node first for multi-node orders
claims.corroboration: Verified from allocation rule change record; change review passed and regression suite was green
claims.limitation: Timing correlation (v18 live → stuck orders 6 hours later) is suggestive but not discriminating

claims.statement: Inventory Control reconciliation shows allocation totals are correct; no obvious issues on their side
claims.corroboration: Direct statement from Inventory Control incident channel response
claims.limitation: Tier 2 trust; 'nothing looks wrong' does not rule out downstream processing failure or carrier integration lag

claims.statement: Other nodes are operating normally; only east node is affected
claims.limitation: Confirms node-specific issue; consistent with v18's east-node-first behavior being the trigger

claims.statement: There is an observability gap: dashboards cannot show how a booked pickup relates to carrier confirmation
claims.corroboration: Observability team verified that Inventory Control cannot see carrier-side records
claims.limitation: Identifies a diagnostic blind spot; does not explain current stuck state but limits root cause attribution

contradictions.claim_a: Allocation reconciliation is correct (C4) and regression suite was green (C3)
contradictions.claim_b: All stuck orders are split-reservation exceptions flagged by v18 (C2)
contradictions.description: If v18 is working correctly (green regression, reconciliation correct), why are split-reservation exceptions causing orders to jam the system? Possible resolutions: (a) regression suite did not cover multi-node split scenarios, (b) exception handling downstream of allocation has a bug, (c) carrier integration is not completing handoff for exception-flagged orders, (d) v18 behavior is correct but the downstream queue processing is broken
contradictions.discriminating_evidence_needed: Diagnostic data on: (1) allocation exception queue depth and age, (2) whether exception-flagged orders reach carrier feed/pickup scheduling, (3) carrier-side confirmation status for these 186 orders, (4) dock readiness and capacity at east node

capability_gaps.reason: Need to verify whether inventory drift could explain the exception flagging, despite Inventory Control's reconciliation claim
Need to understand the exception queue: are these orders stuck in exception handling, or past it?
Need to verify east node dock readiness and capacity; 'nothing obvious' from Carrier Ops is insufficient given the scale (186 orders)
Need to verify whether our 'allocated awaiting pickup' matches carrier's state (pickup booked vs. pending vs. rejected)

next_action.rationale: The core contradiction is whether the allocation rule is functioning correctly (regression passed, reconciliation correct) or whether v18 has a latent bug in multi-node split handling. Auditing allocation exceptions will show whether exception-flagged orders are queued upstream or progressing downstream. This discriminates between an allocation-layer bug (stuck in queue) vs. a carrier integration or dock issue (past allocation, stuck at handoff).
next_action.expected_information_gain: Determines whether the root cause is in allocation rule processing or in downstream carrier integration/dock handling
